scope: 12 canonical workshop/trial screens and 7 extra runtime states at all 5 prescribed sizes
method: Each listed PNG was opened with view_image and inspected as actual pixels. All 12 corresponding source sketches and the 3 updated modular assembly sheets were also opened. SHA256 and capture metadata below bind the review to the inspected artifacts; file existence alone was not used as visual evidence.
acceptanceMeaning: No open P1/P2 visual regressions in the inspected runtime states after the focused-trial correction. This is a technical visual review, not a claim of pixel identity or human art-direction approval.

resolvedFindings.finding: The first capture set cut remote tower assemblies and their wide low bases against the focused viewport's left border, most visibly at 1920x1080, 1600x900 and 1280x960.
resolvedFindings.resolution: The parent corrected focused presentation to omit an out-of-focus assembly as a whole rather than draw a half base. Camera focus and physical actor scale remain separate from overview presentation.
resolvedFindings.recheck: All 5 corrected focused captures and all 5 overview captures were physically reopened. No cut actor or base remains at the viewport border in the focused captures. Overview still presents the complete groups.

sharedObservations: Blue pen outlines, ivory squared paper, hand-drawn typography, restrained gold accents and hatching consistently follow the source visual language.

The low Standard foundation stays a shallow slab; the two distant mounting discs remain legible and the moving weapon silhouette is clear above the mounting cylinder. The two-gun review composition has no visible joint gap or roof occlusion of the mechanisms.

Working runtime numbers were reviewed for visible labels and fit. They were not replaced with illustrative source numbers. Numeric correctness beyond the visible known fixture values is covered by the parent's separate automated checks.
Clipped portions of scrollable off-screen catalog cards are normal viewport behavior. Selected details and primary actions stay visible.
Most screens use the common live workshop header and footer rather than reproducing the source's different per-screen header controls.

The updated modular sheets are authoritative for component silhouettes. Earlier round high tower foundations in sketches 04, 05, 08 and 30 are therefore represented by the current modular foundation, not reproduced literally.
sharedResiduals: The art is assembled from 2D sprites. Perspective, proportions, isolated component cut edges and exploded spacing are not a pixel-identical reconstruction of the paintings.

Large standalone weapon previews expose a small ivory rectangular source/crop fringe beneath the mounting cylinder, clearest in magazine previews. It does not hide a joint, label or control, but remains a polish difference from the surrounding paper.
Peripheral scenery is reused and more subdued than the bespoke scenery painted for several source sketches.
Some secondary long recipe or catalog captions shorten at 1024 pixels; the selected title, cost/availability and main metrics remain available in the primary panel.

Both labelled mounting arrows, all four foundation metrics (2, 10, 55 HP, 16 strokes), prices/level requirements and navigation are visible at every size.
The Standard base is a thin one-course diamond slab with no towering front wall; its complete silhouette fits the hero preview.
residuals: The live current modular low slab differs from the old round masonry concept; the full hero is smaller within the taller 4:3 preview area.

The selected gun seats on the left mount; the empty right seat remains visible and the hero stays inside its allocated area.

The small recipe summary beneath the hero is shortened at narrow widths; the five part tabs remain available.
